name: Emberlace Systems
sovereign_territory: No consolidated physical territory — Emberlace's sovereign claim is distributed across 4,200 infrastructure nodes embedded throughout the GLMZ corridor, including traffic management cores, flood control systems, atmospheric processors, and power routing hubs. Their administrative headquarters, called the Switchboard, is a mobile platform that rotates between three undisclosed locations.
founding_story: Emberlace was formed in 2135 through the forced merger of eleven failing municipal infrastructure agencies whose contracts were acquired by the GLMZ Corridor Authority before the Authority itself was dissolved and its assets privatized. The resulting entity inherited operational control of critical corridor infrastructure before it had a business model, a name, or a permanent leadership structure. Current executive director Tannis Okwuosa, appointed in 2140, is credited with transforming what was essentially a government liquidation asset into the corridor's third-largest corponation by valuation.
security_force: The Conduit — 11,200 personnel with a unique operational structure: two-thirds are cybersecurity and infrastructure defense specialists, one-third are conventional armed response. The Conduit's primary mandate is protecting Emberlace's distributed node network from physical and digital attack. They are authorized to execute infrastructure lockdown protocols that can isolate entire districts from power, water routing, and traffic management — a capability that makes them one of the most feared security forces in the corridor regardless of headcount.
key_detail: Emberlace holds operational contracts for life-critical infrastructure serving approximately 34 million corridor residents. Their adaptive load-balancing AI, called the Weave, makes 1.4 billion autonomous infrastructure decisions per day. In 2147, a 90-second Weave malfunction caused a cascading failure that left 6 million residents without power, water pressure, and traffic signal control simultaneously — an event called the Tangle that resulted in 340 deaths and a Φ2.2 billion settlement that Emberlace paid without admitting fault.
relationship_to_big_20: Big 20 member, ranked approximately 4th by systemic importance though 9th by valuation. Every other Big 20 corponation's physical operations depend on Emberlace-managed infrastructure to some degree. Emberlace's distributed sovereignty model makes it uniquely difficult to threaten, sanction, or acquire — to harm Emberlace is to harm the infrastructure it runs, and no corponation has yet been willing to accept that collateral cost.
full_text: Emberlace Systems Adaptive Infrastructure Corponation — stock designation EMBL, known as Emberlace, The Lace, or simply Ember — holds the distinction of being the only Big 20 corponation with no fixed sovereign territory. Instead, Emberlace's sovereignty is distributed across 4,200 infrastructure nodes embedded throughout the GLMZ corridor: traffic management cores, flood control systems, atmospheric processors, power routing hubs, and dozens of other critical systems serving approximately 34 million residents. Their administrative headquarters, the Switchboard, is a mobile platform rotating between three undisclosed locations as a security precaution. Emberlace did not begin as a visionary enterprise. It was assembled in 2135 from eleven failing municipal infrastructure agencies whose contracts were absorbed by the GLMZ Corridor Authority during a period of governmental collapse, then privatized when the Authority itself was dissolved. The resulting entity inherited operational control of critical corridor systems before it had a name, a leadership structure, or a coherent business model. Executive director Tannis Okwuosa, appointed in 2140, is the architect of what Emberlace became: the corridor's third-largest corponation by valuation at Φ3.6 trillion, generating Φ520 billion annually across 93,000 employees. The Weave, Emberlace's adaptive load-balancing AI, makes 1.4 billion autonomous infrastructure decisions daily. In 2147, a 90-second Weave malfunction produced the Tangle — a cascading failure stripping 6 million residents of power, water pressure, and traffic control simultaneously, resulting in 340 deaths and a Φ2.2 billion settlement paid without admission of fault. Security is managed by the Conduit, 11,200 personnel with the authority to execute district-level lockdown protocols cutting power, water, and traffic management to defined geographic zones — a capability that makes Emberlace functionally immune to physical coercion. No Big 20 actor has yet found a way to threaten Emberlace without threatening the infrastructure they all depend on.

glmzTerritory.description: No consolidated physical territory. Distributed sensor network spanning the entire GLMZ — sovereign claim consists of the sensor installations plus a 10-meter exclusion radius around each. Headquarters in Kenosha interior, Zone 7. Sells environmental, structural, and atmospheric data to all GLMZ corponations simultaneously, maintaining technical neutrality that has survived three major corponation conflicts.
glmzTerritory.grayZoneRelationship: Sensor arrays blanket Gray Zones as thoroughly as corponation territories. Emberlace does not share Gray Zone sensor data with corponations without Gray Zone council consent — this policy has been tested twice in arbitration and held both times.
